Voters split on another election if coalition talks fail

en.title: Spain heads into weekend with snap election as turnout seen at record 75%
en.dek: Polls open Sunday as the center-right People's Party seeks to unseat Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez after eight years of Socialist rule.
facts: Turnout could reach a record 75% in Sunday's snap election, according to Ipsos research director Paco Camas
Polls predict the center-right People's Party will claim victory and potentially topple Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez
A PP-Vox coalition would mark the first time the far right has governed in Spain since Francisco Franco's death in 1975
The Basque Country election risks pushing Catalan independence back onto the political agenda
Vox is on track to double its 2023 seat count from 33 to potentially 66 seats in Congress
body: Spain is heading into the weekend with bated breath as Sunday's snap election could see the country swing to the right after eight years of Socialist rule, Politico Europe reported. Ipsos' director of research in Spain, Paco Camas, told POLITICO's Madrid Playbook that turnout could reach a record 75%. And for good reason: There's a lot at stake.

While polls predict the center-right People's Party will claim victory and -- with help from the far-right Vox -- topple one of the EU's last remaining socialist leaders, Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez still harbors hopes of holding them off. If a PP-Vox coalition comes to fruition, it'll mark the first time the far right has governed in Spain since the death of dictator Francisco Franco in 1975.

The election is also set to reshape politics in the northern industrial region of the Basque Country, where the bitterly divisive question of independence is boiling up again. Despite a likely right-wing coalition on the cards at the national level, polls in the Basque region project a strong electoral performance by the left-wing separatist EH Bildu coalition.
en.context: Spain holds a snap general election on Sunday that could end eight years of Socialist rule under Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, with the center-right People's Party expected to perform strongly, possibly in coalition with the far-right Vox party.

zh.title: 西班牙周末进入提前大选 预计投票率将创纪录达75%
zh.dek: 投票于周日开启，中右翼人民党力图在社民党执政八年后下台
facts: 投票率可能在周日提前大选中达到75%的历史新高，据伊普索研究总监帕科·卡马斯称
民调预测中右翼人民党将取得胜利，并可能推翻社会党总理佩德罗·桑切斯
人民党与极右翼沃克斯组成联盟将标志着弗朗哥死后首次有极右翼在西班牙执政
巴斯克地区选举可能把加泰罗尼亚独立议题重新推上政治议程
沃克斯有望在国会席位从2023年的33席翻倍至可能的66席
body: 西班牙将在周末的关注中迎来大选，周日提前大选可能在执政八年的社会党执政后，使国家向右转向。据欧洲政报报道，西班牙Ipsos研究主管帕科·卡马斯告诉POLITICO的马德里播报，投票率可能达到75%的历史新高。原因很简单：利害关系重大。
虽然民调预测中右翼人民党将获胜，并凭借极右翼人民党的帮助推翻欧盟剩余社会党领袖之一的首相佩德罗·桑切斯，但桑切斯仍抱有阻挡他们的希望。如果人民党与极右翼形成联盟，将标志着弗朗哥独裁政权倒台后，极右翼首次在西班牙执政。
此次大选也将重塑北部工业地区巴斯克自治区的政治格局，那里关于独立的争议性问题再次升温。尽管全国层面可能出现右翼联盟，但巴斯克地区的民调预测，左翼分离主义联盟EH Bildu将取得强劲的选举成绩。
zh.context: 西班牙将于周日举行提前大选，这可能在执政八年的桑切斯社会党政府之后结束，预计中右翼人民党将表现强势，或与极右翼沃克斯党组成联盟。
zh.imageCaption: 支持者在巴塞罗那西班牙总理佩德罗·桑切斯的竞选集会前坐在写有“我真的会投给你”标语前。摄影：Josep Lago/AFP通过Getty Images
